comment: I am a finance major. Environmental Science was not a priority for me but I fulfilled all the requirements and put in a good deal of effort on all assignments given. If any of his classes are not your main focus he will give you a bad grade. It felt like I was fighting an uphill battle from the beginning. Terrible Professor, do not take his classes
Smallwood is a nice person, but his class was so boring. The lab was just an extension of lecture. He was very accessible outside of class to help if you have questions.

Professor Smallwood is knowledgeable and experienced about the subject. There are some readings before every class and a final paper. He is accessible and his grading is reasonable. Didn't find the class to be too difficult.

DO NOT TAKE. Prof. Smallwood makes the class so difficult for everyone. His exams are impossible to do well on and the class average was almost always around a 60%. His lectures are extremely boring and he expects you to know all of the random information he says and the entire textbook. Constantly confused. Made me reconsider my major.

Smallwood is the worst professor at Richmond, he grades horribly, expects you to teach yourself, and is terribly boring. DO NOT take his bio class unless you want to lose all interest in biology and genuinely fail his class. The tests have no correlation to information learned in class and he expects you to memorize the whole textbook.

This class just simply should not be allowed at this school. For how much money the students pay, nothing is learned and he is an awful teacher. He expects you to know everything about plants and animals and doesn't explain anything effectively.

Makes you feel completely inept. Is obviously interested in the material, but fails to make information accessible outside of class, is unclear on grading rubrics, and never curves even when the average is absurdly low. Made me doubt interest in the subject, grade based on few assessments, for your sanity- don't take this course.

I enjoyed class with Professor Smallwood. He has a lot of great personal knowledge from experience that applies to class. He cares about his students not just in class, but their lives outside of class as well.

Terrible professor. Graded by very few things that do not have detailed rubric. Nothing is available after class is done so if you don't take notes, you're screwed. The notes you take barely matter anyway because the stuff he "lectures" about shows up for about 25% of the test, and the rest is never taught. Avoid. Considered switching majors.

9 chapters. 1 test. Thats right. The first test covered 9 whole chapters. He expected us to memorize countless numbers of phyla and subphyla on top of that. His teaching style isnt truly teaching. He makes you read the chapter then cold calls people in class to see if they read the night before. He doesnt lecture. I used to love biology... :(

Dr. Smallwood is passionate, but doesnt execute well. I think the issue is that he's old fashioned. He didnt use PowerPoint so there's no way to access things after class, his grading is inconsistent and he assigns way too many things for the type of class that it is. If we meet on T/TR, I shouldn't have things due for your class every weekday smh

I had Dr. Smallwood in the past, and his class was so boring and difficult that it made me consider dropping my science major. He lectures all class, often without writing anything down. When you get to his tests, they have very little to do with the material he taught you. If you're a freshman taking him, don't let him make you drop science!

He is definitely the professor that I want. He is very passionate and decisive in what he is teaching and he cares about his students very much. As an international student, I always get extra help and understanding from him. He explains things very well. Although the material is hard, I got a 94 on the second test which is not impossible. TAKE HIM

10/10 would recommend Smallwood in a personal setting but not so much in an academic one. Tests do not align with what is taught in class. He taught an excessive amount of material in class and introduced completely new material on exams. To make matters worse he gives zero helpful feedback on work. But he is passionate and cares about students.

Dr. Smallwood is an interesting man, with cool stories about his time in Afghanistan. His tests are long (3 hours) and difficult. He would always answer questions if asked. Few grades. The material for Biodiversity & Conservation Biology was dry and the lectures were sometimes boring. However, the lab section was fun; you get to catch turtles!!
If Smallwood is the professor I'd highly recommend not signing up for the class. His style of teaching is incomprehensible and then he assigns these extremely difficult exams. He will tank your GPA.

Games animals play. It's co-taught by Kerchkove and they both are enthusiastic about the class. It is not your typical FYS. The papers are science based and involve mathematical models. If you are a science student, you will find this class easy, but anyone can get an A if you pay attention and meet with the teachers about your papers.
Make your schedule to avoid his class. He is not good at explaining the material.

Loved his class. I can see how some people thought lectures were boring. Also some people seemed to not get the concept of lines and graphs and really struggled. If you can read graphs, you should be good. Oh, and read the book.

Smallwood is an awesome person, and is super into biology. Unfortunately, his lectures are hard to follow/kind of boring. For the tests, you don't really know what to expect. If you take behavioral ecology, beware, it is kind of all over the place. Pay attention to the graphs and actually read the book.
Go to his office hours. Seriously, don't hand in homework late.

He led me to believe I had a B+ in his class and then I received a C in the class with no explanation.  His lectures are brutal and have nothing to do with the topics you write your papers on.  Learned absolutely nothing.
He's really nice, but he doesn't make sense and just confuses the class. He tries, though. A for effort

Conservation biology may be the bane of my existence but honestly Doc Smallwood's a pretty chill guy. Wears a ponytail and little toe shoes. Has a real passion for biology and will stay with you after class till real late. He's not the most interesting, but just pay attention, read and take notes and you'll do fine.

Super super nice guy. Really wants to help you understand the material. Sometimes his lectures go off on tangents, but they are fun tangents. Really interesting courses and material. Tests are hard, but not impossible.
Sometimes goes to much out of the way. He is willing to help and not much strict in paper's deadline. But seems have a strict requirement on writing style.
It is super hard to get a good greda in his class. Maybe you think you did well in the class, but you are still gonna get a low grade for no reason!!!!!

Took behavioral ecology with him - quite possibly one of the worst professors I've ever had at UR. Nice guy, but so awkward & made no sense. Review sessions useless - often changed what he taught us in class. Everyone was confused, tests ridic & stupid. It should say something when the majority of the class failed his first class. AVOID AT ALL COST

Professor Smallwood sucked, he is very unclear about what he wants, and his labs are pointless. He tries to make jokes which suck, half of the class was sleep before he finished saying his first 5 words. for Tests he does skew the class average so it's easy to get a C on a test.  Avoid him if you can, he put us out in poison ivy, enough said.
Prof. Smallwood's behavioral ecology class was the best science class I took at UofR.  Ridiculously interesting guy, worth getting to know (when he's not off in Iraq or Afghanistan).

The tests were ridiculous and the class average ranged in the high D to low C range. He never scaled his exams which was pathetic. The labs, often done on the computer, were extremely boring. Smallwood should not teach a 100-level course or stick to his stupid obsession with squirrel research that he bores his class with. He sucks. Avoid him.
IMPOSSIBLE TESTS.  HE DEFLATES GRADES TO MAKE SURE THE CLASS HAS A C AVERAGE.  EVERYONE IN MY CLASS HATED HIM.

Great teacher. very interesting even if you dont like ecology. his tests are a little hard but there isnt homework. labs get a little boring. nonscience majors should consider this class over chem or physics
No Comments
